entities.name: Hymns of Enheduanna
entities.label: Text
entities.summary: A collection of 42 temple hymns and personal devotional poems composed by Enheduanna (fl. c. 2285–2250 BCE), high priestess of the moon god Nanna at Ur and daughter of Sargon of Akkad. Enheduanna is the earliest known author in human history whose name is recorded. Her most famous works — "The Exaltation of Inanna" (Nin-me-šára), "Inanna and Ebih," and the 42 Temple Hymns — combine passionate personal devotion with sophisticated theological reflection, establishing models for religious lyric poetry that persist through the Psalms and into modern hymnody.
